scope: Eight priming/contact/costimulation source paths at both pins, plus two whole embedding parents and complete original-to-later differences. Source-asset teaching and bounded parent context, not a replacement ordinary-lesson inventory.

units.requirement: A naive T cell already has its receptor before the illustrated priming encounter; this is not creation of a new receptor designed for the tumor.
Peptide-HLA on an antigen-presenting cell and the T-cell receptor supply the antigen-specific recognition interaction in the illustrated conventional priming model.
CD80/CD86 on the presenter and CD28 on the T cell supply a separate example of supporting receptor contact, rather than another TCR target.

Signal-three cytokine exposure is another interaction influencing growth, differentiation and function; IL-12 and type I interferons are scoped examples for naive CD8 systems, not nutritional fuel or a universal cytokine prescription.
Division or expansion and development of cytolytic function are distinct outcomes that need separate measurement.

In the fictional matched-antigen/costimulation cultures, both divide three times but only B kills suitable targets above target-only background. Equal divisions do not establish equivalent function, the cause of the difference, or clinical benefit.
The three-signal framework is not a literal independent-button or universal binary checklist; timing, prior cell state and inhibitory context matter.
Priming an initially naive cell is different from tumor display, access and recognition at a later effector encounter. Presenter support and tumor target display answer different questions.
Successful priming or stronger stimulation does not by itself establish safe tumor killing or patient benefit, and does not justify indiscriminate removal of inhibitory regulation.

Controlled priming comparisons need a defined starting population, presenting system, antigen/HLA setup, viable-cell input, matched times and appropriate controls; response failure and assay failure remain alternatives.
The A and B contact scenes hold peptide-HLA/TCR recognition constant while the depicted CD28-supporting contact differs.
An omitted supporting interaction in panel B is not an expression measurement establishing that the T cell lacks CD28 or that a marker-negative state has been diagnosed.
CD28 is one costimulation example, rather than the entire molecular category or the only possible signal-two route.
CD28 and CTLA-4 can share CD80/CD86 partners while performing different regulatory jobs; TCR recognition is a separate interaction.
CTLA-4 can capture/remove CD80/CD86 from opposing presenting cells into the CTLA-4-bearing cell and reduce shared ligand availability; the schematic does not establish universal complete shutdown.
Supporting signaling changes the context of response without rewriting the antigen-recognition rule or proving tumor specificity.
Signal two is not a universal binary threshold. Signal strength, duration, state, location and inhibitory inputs affect the response.
Blocking inhibition and adding costimulation are distinct interventions; the diagram does not instruct removal of every brake or predict safe treatment benefit.
Matched recognition-only and supporting/inhibitory perturbation comparisons need measured division, cytokine or killing outcomes; marker abundance alone does not identify the causal interaction.
CD28 dependence of PD-1-blockade rescue in specified experiments and associated lung-cancer observations is not a universal stand-alone CD28 treatment-selection assay.
